description: End-of-life dates for the Python versions, base operating systems and SDK release series the container images use, read by scripts/release/eol.py and rosetta-api/tests/unit/test_base_image_eol.py. A month-only date means the first day of that month. An image fails the guard from 12 months before the earliest end of life of its Python or its base OS.

python.cross_check: https://endoflife.date/api/python.json (fetched 2026-10-27; gives the last day of each scheduled month, e.g. 3.11 2027-10-31)
python.note: Month-only dates are scheduled and can be adjusted (devguide). 3.10 and earlier have exact days.

debian.note: eol is the end of Debian LTS, whose updates go to the same debian-security archive the images use, for amd64 and arm64. regular_support_end is the end of the Debian security team's support. The LTS wiki gives bookworm's LTS period as starting 2026-06-11; debian.org/releases gives regular support to 2026-07-11.

nginx.note: nginx publishes no end-of-life dates. Fixes ship only as new releases of the current mainline (1.31.8 on 2026-10-27) and stable (1.30.6) branches; a branch ends when the next one starts. The nginx images are judged by their Alpine release.

qiskit.note: After a new major release the previous series gets at least six months of bug fixes and one year of security fixes; patch releases go only to the most recent minor version of a supported series. Reported, not enforced: the SDK versions are what the images measure, and changing one is an owner decision.

no_published_window.note: SDKs in the locks for which no end-of-life schedule was found on 2026-10-27 (not each checked at source): pytket, PennyLane, cirq, qsimcirq, qibo, qrisp, quimb, myqlm, pyquil, torchquantum, torch, qulacs, pyquest, pyzx, bqskit, mqt.qmap, numpy, scipy, fastapi, starlette.
